title: Construct and price a reversible P104 residue extractor
body:
PR3035 gives a 343-bit coupled residue domain for rank-seven P104 lifting. Its exact triangular reference has a large intermediate bound and leaves a narrow reversible implementation unpriced. This package constructs an exact reversible residue XOR oracle: **32,417 CNOT + 62,834 Toffoli**, a 1,024-bit clean work bank and two reusable clean adder bits. Quotients remain in the work bank until literal uncomputation; the reducer work words stay four bits.

The all-input triangular lemma assumes `16 Z^256` lies in the pinned HNF lattice, which is checked exactly. The arbitrary target is updated by XOR, signed source inputs are retained, and all clean work returns to zero. Same-H reversal concerns this reducer; an inverse lifting split still needs the separate image lattice `U Gamma`.

The complete static invoice comparison reaches a scoped stop: with the same fixed-width scalar pair loops, coupling retains all 448 narrow lifts and adds this reduction, an ideal pass and recombination. No improvement to that frozen static invoice, general circuit lower bound, runtime claim, admitted supplier or new kappa follows. A changed consumer must identify enough removed work to pay the complete extraction and restoration bill.

Validation: registered Python 3.12 replay; direct optimized Python 3.14 verifier and all eight behavioral groups; exact 170-matrix/8,660-input census; all 340 elementary adders at widths 1..4; signed lifting comparisons through 4,096 bits; literal CNOT/Toffoli oracle; missing-period, wrong-order, quotient-loss, dirty-work, source/typed-receipt and read-only Git-free controls. A separate internal mathematical specialist rederived the proof and gate counts. Warnings-as-errors compilation passes; optional Ruff was unavailable. Hosted CI, human review and formal-kernel proof are separate.

Reproduce:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-modular-residue-reducer
```

Scope is **changed** from the catalogue's `p104-side-correction` card to the concrete numerical-interface handoff from PR3035. Cheap narrow correction is a missing cost obligation of that mechanism; this result tests it without repeating the endpoint-matching census. The [package next questions](https://github.com/RossRichardson/integer-mult-bounds/blob/research/sprint-20261016T195730Z/research/p104-modular-residue-reducer/README.md#open-next-questions) identify a changed consumer or separately priced inverse lattice as the remaining steps. No further construction campaign is proposed.

Only `research/p104-modular-residue-reducer/` is added. Base main `d8e0f83f00191df62174b641e9fff055c357f641`, priority 6 and selected record unchanged at submission refresh. PR3035 `0cc430349a3f3dc200666bc22e997076e0a557ed` and PR3033 `b12bbaeb5ca2e83f15433fc2dd0ba3b766595281` remain pinned. The complete overlap snapshots cover 282 open PRs, 1,776 Discussion records and 2,440 closed PRs with non-atomic timing and no arbitrary-diff/unpublished-work coverage. PR3037's period theorem is a distinct claim, not a dependency used here. [Canonical investigation](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2750#discussioncomment-18982123).

Credit Nick Petalas/PR3035, Tekalign/PR3025/3033, ywz65/PR2586, Arham Tahir/PR2999 and the retained P104/native lineage. Prepared for Ross Richardson with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. Generic modular reduction and reversible adders are not claimed as new. No selected-frontier, priority, shared-checker, frozen-source or other PR disposition change.

One opt-in additive research package with exact source provenance and bounded local replay.
